title: Priority Decoder for Enterprise Logging & PII Request Workflow
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal:
Establish a single, actionable triage and prioritization framework (the "Priority Decoder") for non-bug customer requests related to logging redaction, retention, PII handling, and audit exports. The Decoder should produce: a routing decision (owner/team), an SLO tier, an initial engineering effort bucket, and an escalation path for legal/compliance/infra.

Scope:
- Customer-initiated requests for log redaction, log retention changes, PII-removal requests, structured audit export formats, and related governance controls.
- Excludes incident-driven post-mortems, active security incidents, and feature requests unrelated to data controls.

Deliverables:
1) Priority Decoder matrix (scoring) with weights for: data sensitivity, regulatory scope, user scale affected, retention window change magnitude, required infra invariants (search/index rebuilds), and SLA requirement.
2) Standardized intake form template (support + CSM) with mandatory fields for automated scoring.
3) Routing rules to owners: Platform Security (KMS/audit), Observability Eng (logs infra), Runtime Eng (KV cache & tokenization), Privacy Ops (legal/compliance liaison), and Solutions Eng for customer coordination.
4) Three SLA tiers with response/ack windows and commit windows: Tier A (24h ack / 7d commit), Tier B (3d ack / 30d commit), Tier C (10d ack / >30d commit or roadmap).
5) Runbook snippets and escalation playbook for high-urgency regulatory holds.

Constraints & tradeoffs considered:
- Automation vs. manual review: aim to automate ~70% of incoming requests. Exceptions (sensitive PII removal across multiple exports) require human review.
- Quick fixes vs. correct fixes: temporary redaction entries (e.g., token-level masking) vs. durable schema migration; avoid repeated one-off changes that increase technical debt.
- Privacy risk vs. customer SLA: prioritize regulatory holds and data subject requests above performance-optimization retention changes.

Scoring prototype (abstract):
- Sensitivity: PII/SSN/CreditCard = 50, Pseudonymous = 20, Non-PII = 0
- Regulatory scope: SOC2/GDPR/CCPA = 30, Contractual only = 15, None = 0
- Scale affected (# of users/datasets): >100k = 15, 1k-100k = 8, <1k = 3
- Infrastructure impact: Requires reindex/reprocess = 20, Config change only = 5
- Customer SLA request (explicit): High = 30, Medium = 15, Low = 0
Total score maps to SLA tiers: 80+ => Tier A, 45-79 => Tier B, <45 => Tier C.

Integration points & artifacts linked:
- Intake form draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/EDC-Priority-Decoder-Draft
- Intake automation spec (Webhook + Lambda prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/edc-intake-proto/pull/12
- Example dashboard for request distribution: https://datadog.com/dashboards/edc-priority-decoder

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form deployed to support portal and produces a computed priority field on new tickets.
- Routing rules create a Slack channel/notify owner group based on computed owner.
- SLA tier assignment is visible on the ticket and triggers the correct response timer.
- Documentation and runbook published; initial triage automation covers >=70% of tickets in 2-week pilot.

Risks & mitigation:
- False positives in automation (overclassifying low-impact work as Tier A): include a 24h human verification window for any auto-assigned Tier A.
- Engineering surge from Tier A churn: limit Tier A auto-commits to contractual/regulatory requests only; others require PM approval.
- Data residency/regulatory ambiguity: route unclear cases to Privacy Ops and tag for legal review before commit.

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Miguel (assignee) to finalize scoring weights with Privacy Ops (Priya Desai) by 2026-03-08.
- Liam O'Connor and Observability Eng to prototype routing webhook + Slack automation by 2026-03-15.
- Solutions Eng to prepare 3 customer-facing response templates for each SLA tier by 2026-03-18.

Longer-term ideas (out of immediate scope but tracked):
- Auto-generated remediation PRs for config-only retention changes with automated tests.
- A policy-as-code library to codify retention & redaction rules per customer.
- Integration with Dedicated/Private deployments to expose per-tenant retention controls in console.
